issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies numberOfInscribedStudents as int, but the solution implementation declares numberOfInscribedStudents as long. This causes a type mismatch when summing inscribed and guest students in getTotalNumberOfStudents(), which has an int return type in the specification. As written, the solution code would produce a compilation error (lossy conversion from long to int) and conflicts with the UML/tests expecting int.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute type consistent with the problem UML and tests. Change numberOfInscribedStudents from long to int in the solution (and update the constructor parameter, getter, and setter accordingly) so the sum in getTotalNumberOfStudents() remains an int. Alternatively, if large values are required, update the problem statement/UML and method return types to use long everywhere (including getTotalNumberOfStudents() and related methods) so types are consistent.
